Subject: Post-demo: NovaHealth technical onboarding & telemetry requirements

Hi Samira / Ivan —

Thanks for taking the time to meet today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned on scope for the technical workshop:

Summary of discovery (what we heard)
- Primary use case: clinician-facing summarization and structured extraction from patient encounter notes (low tolerance for hallucinations).
- Expected QPS: ~20 req/sec concurrent across several UI routes; peak burst to 60 for scheduled batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p95 for interactive paths.
- Data residency: US-only.

Integration & architecture points to cover in workshop
1) SDK + auth: We recommend starting with Redwood SDK (Node/Python) and API keys with customer-managed KMS for production. Need to confirm if you require mTLS or VPC-only access.
2) Routing and model variants: We'll suggest an A/B route where the low-latency route hits a smaller quantized model for real-time UI, with a higher-quality variant for async batch reranks.
3) Structured output / tool calling: Define the JSON schema for extraction fields and a deterministic tool-call pattern for downstream validation.
4) Embeddings & re-ranker: We'll map the embedding dimensionality and index cadence (real-time vs nightly re-index).
5) Observability hooks (priority):
   - Insert incoming trace_id (X-Request-Trace / rbw-trace-id) to tie UI traces to server-side tokens.
   - Emit per-request latency headers: X-Redwood-Gen-Latency, X-Redwood-KV-Lookup, X-Redwood-Batch-Wait.
   - Structured JSON logs with fields: request_id, trace_id, model_variant, token_count_in/out, batching_window_ms.
   - Sampling strategy for debug-level token dumps (not full content) and retention guidance.

Attachments: I’ve attached the (rough) architecture diagram you mentioned; can you confirm owners of the API gateway and the embeddings index?

Next steps (proposed)
- Action: Technical workshop with Karthik + SE (sergio) — propose Friday 10/16 10:00–11:30 PT.
- Samira/Ivan: share current gateway auth constraints and the compliance scoping doc.
- We’ll draft an initial mutual action plan with milestones for SDK sandbox, observability checks, and a pilot.

If that looks right I’ll send a calendar invite and the workshop agenda.

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks Jordan — useful recap. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Gateway: We manage an API Gateway in front of our apps (CloudOps team). It supports token-based auth and mTLS; for the initial pilot we prefer token auth but will need mTLS for production.
- Embeddings: we currently use 1536-d vectors and FAISS index nightly; re-ranking happens post-hoc in a batch job today. We’re open to moving to near-real-time if the cost profile is acceptable.
- Compliance doc: attached is our SOC readiness checklist (nova-compliance-scq.pdf).

We can do the workshop Friday 10/16 10:00 PT — that works for the dev and CloudOps folks. Please include the CloudOps email alias so they can join.

One ask re: observability — our SRE wants the ability to correlate a UI session to backend tokenization and per-model token spend so they can allocate cost back to product teams. Can you include a proposal for token accounting fields?

Thanks,
Samira

Samira, Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. A couple technical notes ahead of the workshop:

1) Token accounting & logs
- We can emit token_count_in and token_count_out per request in structured logs; if you need cost allocation per product team we should capture a product_id field in the request metadata so indexing can be done downstream.
- For privacy, we will not log raw user content by default; debug dumps are available behind an allowlist.

2) Trace propagation
- Preferred header: rbw-trace-id (UUID v4) propagated from UI through your gateway into Redwood. We’ll add an example mapping to OpenTelemetry conventions in the workshop.

3) Batching & latency headers
- For continuous batching there is unavoidable added latency (batch_wait_ms) when batching to improve throughput. We’ll add the X-Redwood-Batch-Wait and X-Redwood-Gen-Latency headers.

4) Embeddings/re-ranker
- If you’re on 1536-d vectors we recommend starting with our existing embedding model profile (1536 compat) for parity, then evaluate a 1024-d profile for storage reduction if quality holds.

5) Auth options
- Sandbox: API key with scoped role.
- Prod: KMS-backed keys + optional client cert (mTLS). We’ll prepare a checklist for CloudOps.

I’ll draft a short technical agenda and a minimal set of example log lines + header examples to review in the call.

—Karthik
